claims.text: A self-adaptive tribochemically active surface coating will reduce the coefficient of friction of CoCrFeNi during sliding from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The coating will reduce the wear rate of CoCrFeNi throughout the 25–800 °C range.
The coating can be applied through a one-step deposition process.
The as-deposited coating provides a low-friction interface at lower temperatures.
At approximately 700 °C and above, the coating decomposes or reacts to form a lubricious oxide or compound.
A stable, thermally responsive tribofilm develops on the coated surface.
The tribofilm adheres to the CoCrFeNi substrate.
Temperature-triggered reactions release secondary lubricious species that form a protective tribolayer.
The protective tribolayer maintains low friction at high temperature.
The protective tribolayer minimizes wear at high temperature.
The coating will provide especially improved friction and wear performance near 700–800 °C.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi exhibits degraded friction and wear behavior over a wide temperature range, particularly at elevated temperatures.
The intervention is effective under continuous sliding in ambient atmosphere when the coating transformation is reproducible.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the coating forms lubricious phases in situ over the full temperature range, whereas the intervention and mechanism describe the low-temperature state as the as-deposited coating and place formation of secondary lubricious phases only above a temperature threshold.
